description:
Read one page of the leads a filter actually selects — the sample you show a human before they authorise a run.

Use it to answer "which leads is this?" rather than "how many?". A count of 4,000 is not evidence the filter means what the user thinks it means; ten rows of it usually is.

Keyset-paginated: there is no page number. Pass the next_cursor from the previous response to advance. Sort modes are 'recent' (default) and whatever else the endpoint reports; a forged or stale cursor is a 422, not silently page 1.

Reads only — nothing is written and nothing is spent.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page. Omit for the first page.

exclude_without_website.description: Exclude leads with no website at all. Defaults to true.

filter.description: The filter AST — a TREE, never a string. A group is {op:'and'|'or', conditions:[…]}; a condition is {field, operator, value}. `field` MUST be a key from list_bulk_corpus_fields and `operator` one that field's own `operators` list allows — anything else is a 422 naming what was wrong. Call list_bulk_corpus_fields FIRST; do not guess field names. Only meaningful for source_kind='corpus_query'.

job_id.description: Narrow to ONE job inside a campaign.

stages.description: Stages the NEW run would enable: 'spidersite' (crawl the website), 'spiderverify' (verify emails), 'vayapin' (publish a PERMANENT public profile page). Eligibility is scoped to THIS set — a lead missing only VayaPin is still eligible for a VayaPin-only run. At least one stage must leave a trace in the corpus.

workspace.description: Tenant to target (cli_…). Omit to use the active/bound workspace. list_workspaces shows the options.

name: browse_bulk_corpus_leads
